processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Filing creates the powder particles and introduces internal stress that the subsequent anneal removes.

processing_steps.method: wrapped in a copper foil and sealed in a glass tube

processing_steps.atmosphere: high vacuum (10^-5 mBar); sealed glass tube
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Annealed to remove the internal stress generated during the creation of powder particles by filing. The same annealing treatment was applied to all four Fe-Al compositions (Fe-5Al, Fe-6Al, Fe-6.8Al, Fe-9Al) prior to Mössbauer/SAXS.

structures.overall_structure: Disordered ferritic (BCC) Fe-Al matrix containing nano-sized Fe3Al ordered phase (DO3 structure); established for the Fe-6.8Al powder sample by Mössbauer spectroscopy and SAXS.

precipitates.distribution: Nano-sized ordered phase with log-normal size distribution (SAXS local mono-disperse model); for Fe-6.8Al the SAXS data point (Fig. 4, plotted at ~7 wt% Al) lies between 2.5 and 3.0 nm diameter with volume fraction between 0.5 and 1.0%; SAXS volume fractions are lower than the DO3 volume fraction from Mössbauer spectroscopy.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: powder; for SAXS a thin layer of powdered material sandwiched between Scotch Magic tape
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Mössbauer: 57Co (Rh-matrix) source, velocity calibrated by pure iron (α-Fe) foil. SAXS: dual energy Mo-Cr system, q-range 0.0254–10 nm^-1, camera lengths 550 and 2400 mm, measurement time 4–6 h.

magnetic_properties.hyperfine_field_distribution: P(B_hf) described by a superposition of up to 40 sextets (NORMOS fit)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: conventional constant acceleration Doppler velocity drive with 57Co (Rh-matrix) source; transmission geometry; velocity calibrated with pure iron (α-Fe) foil; spectra fitted with the NORMOS program
characterization_methods.purpose: to examine the local atomic configurations of Fe and the formation of ordered phase upon Al addition
characterization_methods.key_findings: With Al addition new, lower hyperfine-field components appear. For Fe-6.8Al five components were deconvoluted (Table 1): 32.68 T (8.55%/7.7%), 30.34 T (45.45%/44%), 27.69 T (23.63%/24.8%), 25.05 T (2.35%/2.6%) and 23.26 T (1.26%/1.4%). The dominant 30.34 T component may correspond to (7Fe+1Al)nn+(6Fe)nnn or to Fe3Al DO3 ((8Fe)nn+(6Al)nnn). A low-intensity peak at ~23 T suggests a possible Fe3Al phase with low volume fraction.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: laboratory-based dual energy Mo-Cr-SAXS system (Xeuss, Xenocs, France); camera lengths 550 and 2400 mm; q-range 0.0254–10 nm^-1; 2D profiles azimuthally integrated using FIT2D; absolute scale via glassy carbon; scattering angle calibrated with Silver-Behenate
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: transmission geometry; measurement time 4–6 h; thin layer of powdered material sandwiched between Scotch Magic tape
characterization_methods.purpose: to quantitatively estimate the size, volume fraction and number density of the ordered DO3 phase
characterization_methods.key_findings: Scattering from the nano-sized ordered phase is observed as a weak peak between q = 0.3–3 nm^-1; SAXS intensity increases with Al content and Guinier regions shift to low q. Fe3Al ordered-phase diameter increased from 2.5 ± 0.15 nm to 3.75 ± 0.2 nm with increasing Al; SAXS volume fractions are lower than the Mössbauer DO3 volume fractions (SAXS senses ordered phase with sharper boundaries).

computational_details.simulation_method: Fitting of the measured Mössbauer spectrum as a superposition of a distribution of sextets (up to 40) to obtain the hyperfine-field probability distribution P(B_hf)

analytical_models.model_name: hyperfine field vs local atomic configuration
analytical_models.equation_role: relates the observed B_hf to the number of Al atoms in the first and second nearest-neighbour shells
analytical_models.model_note: B = B0 − n1·ΔB1 − n2·ΔB2 (Eq. 1); n1, n2 are the numbers of Al atoms in the first and second nearest neighbours; ΔB1 and ΔB2 values taken from Ref. [26].

computational_details.simulation_method: Local mono-disperse model with a log-normal size distribution, fitted to the SAXS intensity profiles I(q) by nonlinear curve fitting
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Glassy carbon used as secondary standard; Silver-Behenate used to calibrate scattering angle
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The fitted curves (solid lines in Fig. 3) agree well with the experimental SAXS intensities.

analytical_models.equation_role: describes the scattering intensity I(q) of the ordered phase
analytical_models.model_note: I(q) = Δρ² d_N ∫ N(r)[V(r)F(q,r)]² dr (Eq. 2); Δρ is the scattering length difference between Fe3Al (DO3) ordered phase and disordered Fe-Al matrix, d_N the number density and V(r) the volume of the ordered phase.

analytical_models.equation_role: normalized number density distribution function N(r) of ordered-phase radius
analytical_models.model_note: N(r) = 1/(r w √(2π)) exp[−(ln r − ln r_p)²/(2w²)] (Eq. 3); real number density distribution is d_N·N(D) with D = 2r.

analytical_models.equation_role: calculates the average size of the ordered phase from r_p and w
form factor of the ordered phase, assumed spherical
analytical_models.model_note: F(q,r) = 3[sin(qr) − (qr)cos(qr)]/(qr)³ (Eq. 5); as q→0, F²→1, and at large q an asymptotic q^-4 Porod behaviour is observed.

unmapped_findings: For the Fe-6.8Al powder sample the dominant Mössbauer component at B_hf = 30.34 T (Area 45.45%, Vf 44%) cannot be uniquely assigned: it may correspond to the local configuration (7Fe+1Al)nn+(6Fe)nnn or to the Fe3Al DO3 phase ((8Fe)nn+(6Al)nnn), because the two configurations give closely spaced peaks (b0047, b0035).

A low-intensity Mössbauer peak at ~23 T (23.26 T, Area 1.26%, Vf 1.4%) observed for Fe-6.8Al is interpreted as a possible indicator of the presence of Fe3Al phase with a low volume fraction (b0047, Table 1).

SAXS-observed volume fractions of the ordered phase are lower than the DO3 volume fraction obtained by Mössbauer spectroscopy, attributed to the fact that SAXS senses only ordered phase with sharper boundaries whereas Mössbauer traces all local environments including those with diffused boundaries (b0050).

The SAXS ordered-phase diameter/volume-fraction values are presented only in Fig. 4, whose x-axis carries points at 5, 6, 7 and 9 wt% Al (no explicit 6.8 point); the Fe-6.8Al data point appears plotted at ~7 wt% Al, so its exact numerical size (~2.5–3.0 nm) and volume fraction (~0.5–1.0%) are figure-read rather than stated in text (figure_004).

The mechanical properties (yield strength, UTS, elongation, strain-hardening rate), grain/crystallite sizes (25.2, 48.3, 102.3 nm), dislocation density, micro-strain, XRD, SEM and tensile results reported in the paper belong to the 98% cold-rolled and 750 °C (5 min/60 min) annealed BULK Fe-6.8Al samples (a different process), NOT to this 600 °C/60 min powder (Mössbauer/SAXS) sample; they were therefore not attributed to this sample.

The TEM dark-field ordered-phase size of 2.1 ± 0.2 nm for Fe-6.8Al (Fig. 6) is from a bulk TEM specimen (ground and twin-jet electropolished), not explicitly the filed powder used for Mössbauer/SAXS, so it is not attributed to this sample.

All four Fe-Al compositions (Fe-5Al, Fe-6Al, Fe-6.8Al, Fe-9Al) received the same 600 °C/60 min powder annealing treatment; the powder samples were annealed solely to remove the internal stress generated during powder creation by filing (b0016).
